properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, hours after the open ladder shipped in #334: *"looking at this from a fresh perspective; how should this have been done or what is the most correct way?"* Nothing here retracts #334 and nothing is planned.

WHAT SHIPPED, so the alternatives are judged against something concrete: `Component.level` is a STRING naming a rung; `Project.decomposition_levels` is a `list:string` ordered bottom-first; rank is `position()` in that list, computed at read time and never stored; an off-ladder name ranks `None` and is reported as `unknown_level`.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE STRONGEST CRITICISM OF WHAT SHIPPED, AND IT IS THE SAME
MISTAKE ONE LEVEL UP
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The fixed enum was rejected because **"atomic" shifts by domain** — a microprocessor chip for aerospace, a code module for software. **The shipped design asserts ONE LADDER PER DESIGN**, which is that same assertion moved up a rung rather than removed. A system-of-systems spanning an airframe and its flight software has TWO natural ladders, and `Project.decomposition_levels` forces them to share one. `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` explicitly reaches "from code projects to biology projects" — a design that spans both is exactly where this bites.

⇒ Per-SUBTREE ladders, not per-design, may be the correct shape. Nothing in #334 forecloses it (the ladder is read through one function, `decomposition_ladder()`), but nothing anticipates it either.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE FIVE SHAPES, WITH WHAT EACH COSTS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**A. DECLARED RUNG NAME (what shipped).** Legible in diffs and messages; no migration (93 components untouched); insertable without renumbering stored data. Costs: a string can be misspelled and the schema no longer catches it; list POSITION is implicit ordering, so inserting a rung silently renumbers every rank; one ladder per design.

**B. DERIVE DEPTH FROM THE SPINE — drop `level` entirely.** Depth = distance from the root of `CONTAINS`. No ladder to declare, no typos, unlimited depth free, and `level_spine_disagreement` becomes IMPOSSIBLE rather than detected.
⚠️ ALREADY CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, and the reason must be read precisely. `cap:ask-for-one-rung-of-the-decomposition` records: deriving the top tier from the spine "returns leaves nobody wired to a parent — measured on this design: 8 subsystems by declared level, 2 leaves by spine position."
⭐ BUT THAT MEASUREMENT IS ABOUT AN INCOMPLETE SPINE, NOT ABOUT DERIVING BEING WRONG. The derived answer was wrong because 14 components had no parent, not because depth is a bad definition of level. **The two failure modes are different and the design pays for one of them today:** derive fails on an unwired spine; declare fails when declaration and spine disagree, which is why `level_spine_disagreement` had to be built at all. Choosing declare bought a detector.
Costs of B that stand regardless: a node not yet wired has NO level, so "this is a subsystem" cannot be claimed before it is placed; and the NAMES carry meaning a reader wants — "subsystem" not "depth 2".

**C. RUNGS AS FIRST-CLASS NODES.** `cmp:x` points at `lvl:subsystem`; rungs order by `PRECEDES` edges. Typos become impossible (edge endpoints are validated), ordering is explicit rather than list position, insertion is a new node plus two edges with nothing renumbered, a rung can carry its OWN description — and Anthony's four stopping rules could attach to the rung they govern instead of living in a fact nobody traverses. Costs: a new node type, an edge per component, heavier queries, and it is the most machinery for a property that is one word.

**D. RELATIVE ONLY — no names, just "a parent is exactly one below its child".** Simplest possible; works at any depth. Loses "show me every subsystem" entirely, which `cap:ask-for-one-rung-of-the-decomposition` was built to provide and which is a real question people ask.

**E. DECLARE AND DERIVE, AND MAKE THE DISAGREEMENT THE PRODUCT.** Keep the declared name AND compute spine depth, then report where they diverge — which is half-built already as `level_spine_disagreement`. This treats the two answers as independent evidence rather than picking a winner. Costs: two things to keep, and it only pays off on a design whose spine is complete enough for the derived answer to mean anything.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY DECIDE IT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Not argument — a measurement nobody has: **how complete is the containment spine on a real design?** `fact:the-black-box-tier-has-two-answers-that-disagree` measured 121 of 2,526 nodes (4%) carrying a CONTAINS parent, and 14 components as roots. If the spine were complete, B costs nothing and removes a whole defect class. While it is 4% populated, B is unusable and A is the only thing that works. **So the right shape depends on a number that moves, and today's number argues for what shipped.**

📌 A SMALLER THING WORTH RECORDING: `list:string` had existed in the schema validator and been used by NO schema file — `Project.decomposition_levels` is its first real use. That is untested territory reached without noticing, and it is the kind of thing that is fine until it is not.

KEPT DISTINCT from `fact:the-black-box-tier-has-two-answers-that-disagree` after reading it: that is the 2026-08-18 MEASUREMENT of the two answers disagreeing, and it is the evidence this reasons FROM. This is the design question that measurement raises and does not answer — which of five shapes should carry depth at all.
properties.name: OPEN — was the open ladder built the right way? A declared rung NAME per component was one of at least five shapes, and the one that shipped still asserts ONE ladder per design
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled, and #334 stands.

Kept separate from `dec:the-decomposition-ladder-is-open-not-a-fixed-enum` (which decided THAT the ladder opens, and is accepted and implemented) and from `cap:ask-for-one-rung-of-the-decomposition` (the built capability whose declare-over-derive choice this re-examines). This asks a third thing neither answers: given that the ladder is open, is a declared rung NAME the right carrier for depth at all — asked with the implementation in hand rather than before it, which is why it can criticise something concrete instead of speculating.
